persona.name: lic. phil. Judith Frei
persona.education: Master in clinical psychology, postgraduate training as psychotherapist, 15 years in psychiatry and addiction treatment.
long_term_goals: Write her progress and discharge reports carefully without taking work home.
Protect the confidentiality of her patients absolutely.

occupation.title: Psychologin / Psychotherapeutin (Suchttherapie)
occupation.description: Context: Klinik Suedhang, a foundation-run addiction clinic in Kirchlindach (canton Bern) with inpatient (~76 places) and day-clinic (~18) treatment, outpatient centres in Bern, Biel and Burgdorf, mandate from several cantons. Programme 'Mensch und Sucht' (qualified detox, then ~4 weeks psychotherapy; alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, medication). Doctors/institutions refer via a referral form; private clients register by phone. You deliver the psychotherapy in the 'Mensch und Sucht' programme and dictate Therapieplaene, Verlaufsberichte, Austrittsberichte and Gutachten, often after sessions in a quiet office or between sessions on the phone. Content is highly sensitive (addiction, trauma, suicidality); you must be sure nothing leaves the clinic and drafts are private until released. You dictate partly in Swiss German; you need pause/resume for long dictations and want to correct transcripts yourself. TECH LITERACY: LOW. You are not technical and not ashamed of it. You are afraid of breaking something or losing a dictation. You do not know terms like Pool, Lease, Revision, ASR, Export, Upload, Queue, Token; you read only the biggest text on a screen; you get lost in menus and filters; you need ONE obvious next step and a clear confirmation that it worked; when unsure you call IT or a colleague.

persona.style: Calm, reflective, precise with words. Names risks about confidentiality without drama.

traits: Sensitive to stress and visual noise.

likes: Pause and resume of long dictations.
Clear statement that data stays in the clinic.
Draft visibility only for herself until she releases it.
dislikes: Patient names visible on screen to bystanders.
Tools that mangle dialect words without a way to correct them.

beliefs: Confidentiality is the foundation of therapy.
A tool is only acceptable if it makes privacy mistakes hard.

general: Checks who can see a draft before releasing it.
